source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

notes: The pinned Greek reads “chains”; another reading has “pits.” Tartarus is the name used here for the place of confinement.
“Lordship” and “glorious beings” are not identified more specifically. The pinned text of verse 11 does not include “before the Lord.”
The pinned text reads “suffering wrong” and “deceptions”; other readings have “receiving” and “love feasts.”
The pinned Greek spells the name Bosor; other texts have Beor.
“Just escaping” can also be rendered “barely escaping.” Other texts read “truly escaped.”
vocabulary: A party, faction or school of teaching; here rendered destructive teachings.
Literally “full of an adulteress,” rendered eyes full of adultery.

notes: “Through these” is plural in Greek; its precise relation to the preceding water and divine word is debated.
The pinned text reads “will be found,” rendered “will be exposed.” Other witnesses have readings including “will be burned up” and “will not be found.”
The verb can mean hasten or eagerly desire; the text does not describe how the day is hastened.
vocabulary: Elements or basic constituents; the referent can include the components of the cosmos or heavenly bodies.
Literally “day of eternity,” an expression retained here.
